chapters.title: The First Night: Deny Trauma
chapters.sourcePressure: The source supports a first night about people not being bound by past experiences, purposive interpretation, fabricated anger, and self-dislike as a protective pattern while warning against denying pain itself.
chapters.coreMove: Treat a painful backstory as context, then ask what the present pattern still accomplishes before granting it authority.
chapters.commonMisread: Trauma is fake, pain is just an excuse, and people can change by deciding to be positive.

chapters.title: The Second Night: All Problems Are Interpersonal Relationship Problems
chapters.sourcePressure: The source supports inferiority as subjective assumption, bragging as tied to inferiority, life not as competition, escalation from power struggle to revenge, and life tasks as a healthier frame.
chapters.coreMove: Notice when another person's movement has been converted into your rank, then return attention to the task instead of the scoreboard.
chapters.commonMisread: Do not compare yourself to others and just feel good about your own path.

chapters.title: The Third Night: Discard Other People's Tasks
chapters.sourcePressure: The source supports not living to satisfy others' expectations, separating tasks, reducing interpersonal problems by clarifying responsibility, recognition as unfreedom, and holding one's own cards.
chapters.coreMove: Sort choice, effort, outcome, and evaluation until approval and disappointment are no longer smuggled into your jurisdiction.
chapters.commonMisread: Set boundaries by caring less and telling people their feelings are not your problem.

chapters.title: The Fourth Night: Where the Center of the World Is
chapters.sourcePressure: The source supports the goal of relationships, not being the center of the world, critique of rebuke and praise, value through contribution, and someone beginning the horizontal shift.
chapters.coreMove: Replace the wish to be central or above with one visible act of horizontal contribution.
chapters.commonMisread: Be humble, be nice, and stop needing attention.

chapters.title: The Fifth Night: To Live in Earnest in the Here and Now
chapters.sourcePressure: The source supports excessive self-consciousness, trust versus confidence, work as contribution, workaholism as life-lie, life as a series of moments, and giving meaning to seemingly meaningless life.
chapters.coreMove: Act from contribution in the present without demanding certainty, image safety, or a finished life story first.
chapters.commonMisread: Live in the moment, follow your heart, and stop worrying about the future.
